title: Sanyo Electric Railway adopts AI crossing cameras after a three-crossing trial
summary: Sanyo adopted Optage’s AI crossing cameras after a 2020 trial. Optage reports comparable function at lower cost than laser radar, without measured accident reduction.
account: Mynavi News reported on 12 Aug 2020, from a press release, a field trial of AI image analysis of crossing surveillance cameras. Optage, Sanyo Electric Railway and the Sanyo Electric Railway Information Center had begun it. It ran from early August to mid-October 2020 at three crossings on Sanyo Electric Railway lines. Edge devices analyze the video in real time to detect people, including those with prams or wheelchairs. They aim to stop trains safely by signaling the driver through a special signal lamp and notifying the operations center over an IP-VPN. Accuracy in rain and at night was to be verified with K4Digital. Full deployment was targeted for spring 2021. No results are reported, and the OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry notes that no incidents had been reported. Optage’s follow-up of June 29, 2021 reports that Sanyo adopted the system after the trial. It reports comparable function at lower cost than laser radar but supplies no numerical detection results or measured reduction in accidents.
purpose: The trial was built to detect people in crossings in real time and alert train drivers.
system: AI image analysis of crossing cameras on edge devices with special-signal-lamp and IP-VPN alerts
deployer: Sanyo Electric Railway and Sanyo Electric Railway Information Center (trial)

fields.account: Mynavi News reported on 12 Aug 2020, from a press release, a field trial of AI image analysis of crossing surveillance cameras. Optage, Sanyo Electric Railway and the Sanyo Electric Railway Information Center had begun it. It ran from early August to mid-October 2020 at three crossings on Sanyo Electric Railway lines. Edge devices analyze the video in real time to detect people, including those with prams or wheelchairs. They aim to stop trains safely by signaling the driver through a special signal lamp and notifying the operations center over an IP-VPN. Accuracy in rain and at night was to be verified with K4Digital. Full deployment was targeted for spring 2021. No results are reported, and the OECD AI Incidents Monitor entry notes that no incidents had been reported. Optage’s follow-up of June 29, 2021 reports that Sanyo adopted the system after the trial. It reports comparable function at lower cost than laser radar but supplies no numerical detection results or measured reduction in accidents.
